source: JZ Mock A · Paper 1 · Question 14 · Publisher worked solution
knowledgePattern: Apply translation, off-axis reflection and horizontal scaling in order

hints.title: Follow one transformation at a time
hints.body: First translate the input and output, writing down the entire new function before moving on.
hints.recap: Horizontal translation changes the input; vertical translation changes the output.
hints.pitfall: A leftward shift has the opposite sign inside the function.

recall.reminder: Horizontal translation changes the input; vertical translation changes the output.

hints.title: Reflect about the stated height
hints.body: Reflecting a point in y=k sends its height y to 2k−y. Apply this to the whole current function.
hints.recap: A reflection preserves the midpoint height on its mirror line.
hints.pitfall: Reflect the translated graph, not the starting graph.
hints.pause: Write the reflected function, then apply the final horizontal scale to its input.

recall.reminder: A reflection preserves the midpoint height on its mirror line.

solution:
1. Let f(x)=2x2−3x+1. Translating left 1 and up 4 gives f(x+1)+4=2x2+x+4.

2. Reflection in y=2 sends a height y to 4−y. Thus the next curve is 4−(2x2+x+4)=−2x2−x.

3. A horizontal scale factor 1/2 replaces the input by 2x. The final curve is −2(2x)2−2x=−8x2−2x. Answer A.
